items.title: 10 Biggest Reveals at Final Fantasy 14's Berlin Fanfest Presentation
items.summary: Do we basically already know both jobs?
items.content:
By Stephanie Watel Published Jul 28, 2026, 1:23 PM EDT Stephanie Watel is a Contributing Writer at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2022. She specializes in guides and reviews, with additional experience writing lists and features across RPGs, horror games, cozy sims, action games, open-world RPGs, JRPGs, and indie titles.

Before joining DualShockers, Stephanie contributed to GameRant , IGN , MovieWeb , Pro Game Guides , Twinfinite , and Prima Games . Her work has covered major releases, underground sleeper hits, and indie games across a wide range of genres. Stephanie holds a B.A. in English , including studies in journalism.

As the months tick by and Final Fantasy 14 's upcoming expansion, Evercold, draws ever closer, the Fanfest circuit brought director Naoki "Yoshi-P" Yoshida and his team to Berlin this month for the second pitstop. Fans on the ground and online have speculated about what could be revealed at this latest showcase to shed more light on Evercold's content and how the game is set to dramatically evolve (for the better) from top to bottom.

Square Enix has announced Beyond the Lifestream, a Final Fantasy 7 Revelation crossover with Final Fantasy 14 that's launching in 2027.

All-new reveals were substantially fewer this time around, though that's entirely acceptable given that Anaheim's keynote basically broke records across the board for the sheer amount of groundbreaking information that fans had to process in the span of two hours. However, nonetheless, Berlin's keynote still brought plenty to the table that helped flesh out the bigger picture for what's to come in Evercold and beyond. There were even some unexpected surprises that kept the conversation buzzing well after the convention floor closed up shop.

The first and probably one of the most hilarious moments and perhaps accidental reveals in the entire keynote dropped about halfway through the presentation, as Koji Fox and Yoshi-P discussed updates to character customization and cosmetics.

For context, during the Anaheim leg of the Fanfest circuit, Yoshi-P and others from the team took part in a dice roll-style Q&A, and one fan question brought up the prospect of a so-called "butt slider" option for character customization. That is, the ability to adjust your character's derrière as you please. This drew a mix of bafflement and confused laughter from Yoshi-P, who cordially brushed it off at the time.

However, it seems that they might actually be taking it seriously, as Koji Fox went out of his way, in the sassiest and most entertaining way possible, to bring it up out of the blue. As he playfully antagonized Yoshi-P about the butt slider that fans clearly yearn for, Yoshi-P seemed to go along with the joke and surprisingly said, "just wait", while then also shushing him, claiming that it's "a secret." As if to play the audience along even further, he even blurted a remark about "long hair", which was also brought up at the dice roll Q&A.

The awkward moment ends there with no further concrete information, but since both Koji and Yoshi-P went out of their way to bring it up, it's evident that both those customization ideas are not off the table with FFXIV's developers. As for when it could realistically happen, while there's honestly no telling, it could possible not to rule out sometime during 8.0's expansion lifecycle. After all, the game is getting a buffet of other customization updates throughout Evercold, and this could ever-so-conveniently...well, slide in there during one patch update or another.

On the back of that hilarious moment was the reveal of even more cosmetic customization options for players to use. As shown in a slideshow of various examples with base character races, upon the launch of Evercold, certain physical features will have a toggle option that helps players customize their character even further from the get-go.

These options include toggling off the facial war paint for Miqo'tes of both genders (seen above), the infamous "nose smudge" for Lalafells and Vieras, and finally making horn styles for Au'Ras interchangeable. Up until now, the latter has especially been a point of contention for players with Au'Ra characters, as certain horn styles have forever been locked to certain preset facial types. If you liked a certain face type, you had to use the default horns they came with, and vice versa.

However, that restriction is now set to disappear come Evercold's launch (technically with Patch 8.1), and that's not counting all of the other customization changes and additions that are in store for the expansion and beyond.

Despite the tragedy that was FF14 Mobile , the news of the game coming to the Nintendo Switch 2 first dropped in Anaheim to much excitement, along with some preliminary details on what to expect when starting a subscription on the handheld console.

The topic came up again in Berlin, starting with a solid launch date of August 4, 2026. With such a quick turnaround on that bit of info, Yoshi-P assured players that the game is set and ready to go, but also gave yet another incentive to get the community comfortably on board. The first month will serve as a testing stage for the game's many servers, and as such, that first month will be free to all subscribed players.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Launches on Nintendo Switch 2 Next Week, Requiring 117.2 GB of Storage
items.summary: Final Fantasy 14 launches on Switch 2 on August 4 with a 117.2 GB file size. Learn about storage needs, microSD Express support and setup checks.
items.content:
Final Fantasy 14 launches on Switch 2 on August 4 with a 117.2 GB file size. Learn about storage needs, microSD Express support and setup checks.

Final Fantasy XIV is finally heading to Nintendo Switch 2 next week , but players may need to clear some serious storage space before entering Eorzea.

Square Enix will release Final Fantasy XIV for Nintendo Switch 2 on August 4, giving players another portable way to access its enormous MMORPG. As spotted on the US eShop , the Switch 2 version comes with a hefty 117.2 GB storage requirement.

That is not a minor download by handheld standards. Nintendo Switch 2 includes 256 GB of internal storage, meaning Final Fantasy XIV alone could occupy nearly half of its total advertised capacity. The system software and any games already installed will reduce the space actually available to players, making the practical situation even tighter.

In other words, you may want to begin cleaning out that backlog now.

Nintendo Switch 2 supports microSD Express cards for expanded game storage, and Final Fantasy XIV is exactly the sort of release that makes one worth considering. A 117.2 GB installation leaves considerably less room for other large games, downloadable content, screenshots, and future updates.

Players should also remember that live-service games rarely remain the same size forever. Final Fantasy XIV regularly receives patches, seasonal content, balance adjustments, and major expansions. Its Switch 2 storage footprint could therefore change after launch, even if 117.2 GB is enough for the initial installation.

Standard microSD cards used with the original Switch cannot store and run Switch 2 software. Anyone purchasing additional storage specifically for Final Fantasy XIV should make sure the card uses the microSD Express standard.

Final Fantasy XIV launches on Switch 2 in 4 editions.

The Switch 2 port is still a major step for the game. Portable access could make crafting, gathering, daily activities, and shorter questing sessions more convenient, provided the version delivers stable performance and readable interface scaling.

Final Fantasy XIV launches on Switch 2 next week.

items.title: Wisdom of Nym: Reactions to Final Fantasy XIV’s second fan festival
Final Fantasy XIV Launches August 4 for Switch 2, Evercold Expansion in January 2027 - News
items.summary: Square Enix announced Final Fantasy XIV will launch for the Nintendo Switch 2 on August 4 and the Evercold expansion [...]
items.content:
Square Enix announced Final Fantasy XIV will launch for the Nintendo Switch 2 on August 4 and the Evercold expansion will launch in January 2027.

Pre-orders for the Switch 2 versions are now open. It will require a separate monthly subscription from the other version, however, it will not require a Nintendo Switch Online subscription. Users subscribed to other platforms can get a 50 percent discount on the subscription price on the Switch 2.

View the Evercold expansion extended trailer below:

Square Enix today revealed brand-new information about Evercold , the sixth expansion for its critically acclaimed MMORPG Final Fantasy XIV Online , set to launch in January 2027 alongside new playable content, a Final Fantasy VII Remake trilogy crossover raid series, the Nintendo Switch 2 version release date, and more.

An extended teaser trailer for Evercold was also revealed, providing a glimpse into the world of the Fourth and the adventures that await the Warrior of Light in the start of the Goddless Realms Saga story arc.

During the Fan Festival 2026 in Berlin keynote address, Producer and Director Naoki Yoshida revealed the first new job coming to Evercold : Bastion—a main tank that wields a pair of greatshields known as skyltborg—and unveiled a trailer showcasing the new job in action.

Details were also shared on several new features coming to Evercold , including changes to the narrative structure that will be implemented for the main scenario, field, and game system, allowing players more freedom to choose what area they complete first between various paths in the main scenario. Through Auto Content Balancing, difficulty scaling and enemy levels will adjust to the appropriate player level as they play through dungeons in their chosen order. Additionally, a first look was provided for Character Action Skins, a feature that lets players assign alternate animations to personalize existing General actions, such as Teleport and Warp, with support for additional skins such as job actions arriving in future updates. Character customization will also be expanded so players have more ways to make their character stand out, including a greater range of color options with the new color picker, the ability to fine-tune features such as eyes and lips, new elements such as eye shadow, and more.

Following the reveal of the Evangelion “Ghosts of Desire” alliance raid series in April, Yoshida unveiled a new teaser trailer and announced that acclaimed director and animator Mahiro Maeda will join the project as a special guest artist and designer. Throughout his career, Maeda has contributed to numerous acclaimed projects, including Mad Max: Fury Road (2015) as a concept artist and designer, and Evangelion:3.0 +1.0 Thrice Upon a Time (2021), where he served as director, concept art director, storyboard artist, art setting designer and key animator.

Joined on stage by Final Fantasy VII Remake series Director Naoki Hamaguchi, Yoshida also revealed “Beyond the Lifestream,” a new Final Fantasy VII -themed eight-player raid series that players will challenge in Evercold . Both development teams are working closely together to create an exciting new raid experience for players.

Further, Final Fantasy XIV will launch on Nintendo Switch 2 on Tuesday, August 4, 2026, with pre-orders starting today on Nintendo eShop. To ensure server stability, there will be an approximately one-month free subscription period on Nintendo Switch 2. Whether beginning with the Free Trial, starting their adventure with the Starter Edition, or diving into the full story and experience with the Complete Edition, more players than ever before will soon be able to join together in the vast world of Final Fantasy XIV .

An outline of the content reveals from the keynote address can be found below:

Finally, Yoshida revealed the Evercold Collector’s Bundle, which includes a collection of physical items: the Evercold Special Art Box, Expertly Crafted Reaper Figure, Ethos Metal Keychain, Köttr Mini Plush, and Tapestry of the Fourth. Also included is the digital Collector’s Edition, featuring three in-game items: the Crystal Skyltborg bastion weapon, Vallhallar Odin mount, and Entreat Crystal emote. More information regarding availability and pre-orders will be announced in the future.

items.content:
The FFXIV Evercold Collector’s Edition includes a transforming mount, Reaper statue, and exclusive items. Here’s everything included.

From a transforming mechanical mount to an exclusive Reaper statue, here is everything included in both versions of the Final Fantasy XIV Evercold set.

During the Final Fantasy XIV Fan Festival 2026 event in Berlin, Square Enix revealed major updates about the popular MMORPG. The Japanese developer announced the FFXIV Evercold Collector’s Edition , which includes a mix of physical goods and several exclusive in-game items.

While we don’t yet have the price, Square Enix gave us several images of the FFXIV Evercold Collector’s Edition. There will be two versions of the CE: an all-digital edition and a physical bundle . For your convenience, here is a breakdown of everything included in both.

Note: We’ll update this list with the official item names when they are revealed.

Square Enix also showed off the new Evercold Valhallar Odin Mount in a trailer posted to X. “Gallop into Evercold on the Collector’s Edition mount.” The trailer shows off the Valhallar Odin with over one minute of new gameplay footage.

Incredibly, the mechanical horse mount can even turn into a full-blown mech. In the trailer, we see an animation where the steed transforms into a mech in real time and lets you fly through the air with it. Yes, you read that right. The Evercold mount lets you ride on the ground and fly through the air. It’s pretty sick.

The FFXIV Evercold release date is January 2027 . At the time of writing, Square Enix has not given us a specific date. However, it will launch sometime during the first month of the year. The expansion is pretty massive and includes new dungeons, an overhauled combat system, as well as the new Bastion Job Class.

Square Enix also finally confirmed that Final Fantasy XIV will launch on Nintendo Switch 2 on Tuesday, August 4, 2026 . This means Switch 2 players will have several months to jump into the MMORPG and catch up before Evercold arrives in January.

With a transforming mount, an impressive Reaper statue, and new artwork from legendary artist Yoshitaka Amano, the Evercold Collector’s Edition looks like a packed release for longtime fans. We’ll update this article as soon as Square Enix confirms its price, preorder date, and final list of items.

items.content:
In the hope that would-be adventurers can experience all that FFXIV has to offer, we are pleased to announce the latest Free Login Campaign. Follow the Trail to the Heavens! In Patch 7.5, you can face Enuo in the Unmaking, take a stroll through Windurst: The Third Walk in the FINAL FANTASY XI alliance raid crossover, and leap into battle in Archeia Harmonias, an all-new arena for Crystalline Conflict. A host of other additions and adjustments will make your time in Eorzea more streamlined and enjoyable, including increased furnishing placement limits, the consolidation of dyes, and additional pieces of gear that can now be converted to outfit glamour or stored in the armoire. With the introduction of Patch 7.5, the Shadowbringers expansion can now be played as part of the FINAL FANTASY XIV Starter Edition. The expansion will be automatically registered to your account if you already own the Starter Edition, so why not take this opportunity to jump into the adventure?

If you or any of your friends are currently taking a break from your adventures, you won't want to miss out on this limited-time event! Visit the Free Login Campaign website for details.
